column3: Retains the active judging and declaring righteous or guilty.
Retains forty as the number of blows, followed by the prohibition on adding.
Retains the firstborn rather than explicitly the first son, and standing for the name.
Retains going up to the gate and raising up a name.
Retains answering and saying and the image of building his brother’s house.
Retains his name rather than explicitly his family name.
Retains a man and his brother without explicitly specifying two; retains the hand of the striker.
Retains your eye as the subject of showing pity.
Retains stone and stone, large and small.
Retains a complete and just stone and ephah in the singular, and your days.
Repeats everyone doing and retains doing these things.
Retains Amalek as a collective singular.
Retains the singular Amalek as the actor.
